matchstick.title: Movable vertical sticks in simple numerals
matchstick.principle: I, II, III, and L can lose or gain a single vertical matchstick while remaining valid Roman numerals (e.g., III → II, II → I, I → II, I → L). This enables value adjustments of ±1.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the equation is off by a small amount (typically 1 or 2) and the numerals involved include I, II, III, or L.
matchstick.example: Changing III + I = V to II + II = V by moving one vertical stick from the first III to the I.

matchstick.title: Preserve source and destination validity
matchstick.principle: After removing a stick, the originating character must still be a recognized Roman numeral or operator, and after adding the stick, the target character must also become a valid numeral or operator. Avoid leaving incomplete shapes.
matchstick.when_to_apply: For any candidate stick move, verify both the source and destination remain valid.
matchstick.example: Moving the I from VI to the right‑hand I yields V (valid) and II (valid).

matchstick.title: Guide moves by numeric difference
matchstick.principle: Compute the numeric values of both sides. The difference indicates how much the total must change. Moving a vertical stick changes a numeral by ±1 (or ±2 when reordering I around V). Use this to target the needed adjustment.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the equation is false and the numeric gap is small (1–2).
matchstick.example: VI = I + III is off by 2; moving the I before V changes VI (6) to IV (4), closing the gap.

matchstick.title: Reordering I around V changes value by 2
matchstick.principle: In Roman numerals, placing I before V (IV) yields 4, while placing I after V (VI) yields 6. Moving a single I across a V therefore changes the value by exactly 2.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the equation involves VI or IV and the discrepancy is 2.
matchstick.example: VI = I + III → move the I before V → IV = I + III (4 = 4).

matchstick.title: Cross‑side vertical stick transfer adjusts both sides by ±1
matchstick.principle: Removing an I from a numeral reduces its value by 1; adding that I to a numeral on the opposite side raises its value by 1. This simultaneous ±1 change can balance equations where one side exceeds the other by 2.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the left side is larger by 2 and both sides contain I‑type numerals.
matchstick.example: VI = I + III → move the I from the left side to the right‑hand I → V = II + III (5 = 5).

matchstick.title: Never take sticks from V or X
matchstick.principle: V and X consist solely of diagonal sticks; removing one leaves a single diagonal stick, which is not a valid Roman numeral. Therefore they cannot serve as sources for a single‑stick move.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When considering a source numeral that is V or X.
matchstick.example: Do not try to take a stick from V to turn it into I.

matchstick.title: Operator validity after stick moves
matchstick.principle: Operators must remain one of the allowed symbols (+, -, =). Removing a stick from '+' turns it into '-', and removing a stick from '=' leaves an invalid single line. Ensure any modification leaves a recognized operator.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When a candidate move involves an operator.
matchstick.example: Removing the vertical from '+' would create '-', which is only acceptable if the resulting arithmetic still holds.

matchstick.title: Final verification of numerals and equality
matchstick.principle: After performing a stick move, confirm that each token is a valid Roman numeral (I, II, III, IV, V, VI, VII, VIII, IX, X, etc.) and that the arithmetic equality is true.
matchstick.when_to_apply: As the last step for any proposed move.
matchstick.example: After moving the I from VI to the right side, check that V = II + III (5 = 2+3) holds.

matchstick.description: Taking a stick from V or X, leaving an invalid shape
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model treats any stick as movable without checking that the source numeral stays valid after removal.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Never use V or X as a source for a single‑stick move; only use numerals that can lose a vertical stick while remaining valid.

matchstick.description: Changing an operator to an invalid one
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model may move a stick from '+' or '=', forgetting that the resulting shape must still be a recognized operator.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: After any stick move involving an operator, verify that the operator is still '+', '-', or '='.

matchstick.description: Assuming a single stick can change a numeral's value arbitrarily
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model overestimates the effect of moving a stick, e.g., thinking it can turn VI into VII directly.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Remember the exact numeric impact: moving an I changes a numeral by ±1; moving an I across a V changes by ±2; other moves have limited effects.

matchstick.description: Neglecting to recompute the arithmetic after the move
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model proposes a visual transformation but does not verify the resulting equality.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Always calculate the numeric values of both sides after the move and confirm the equality holds.

matchstick.description: Treating diagonal sticks as interchangeable with vertical sticks
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model assumes orientation does not matter and rotates sticks arbitrarily.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Respect stick orientation: diagonal sticks can only form V or X shapes; vertical sticks form I. Do not substitute one for the other.
